Chapter 1 — Introduction

Agent kya hota hai, aur is poori book ka map kya hai — agent ki anatomy wali figure poori book ki foundation hai; har aane wala chapter uske ek component ko zoom karke dikhata hai.

Book ki shuruaat ek simple sawaal se hoti hai: ek chatbot aur ek agent me farak kya hai? Chatbot sirf jawab deta hai; agent dekhta hai, sochta hai, aur kaam karta hai — phir us kaam ka result dekh kar agla step decide karta hai. Yahi loop poori book ka centre hai.

Is chapter me kya milega

  • 1.1 Agent ki classic definition — sensors, actuators aur environment.
  • 1.2 LLM — agent ka "brain", jo bas next token predict karta hai.
  • 1.3 Reasoning LLMs — System 1 (fast) vs System 2 (slow, deliberate) soch.
  • 1.4 Memory + Tools — "augmented LLM", agent ka building block.
  • 1.5 Planning aur reflection — yahi cheez LLM ko agent banati hai.
  • 1.6 Autonomy ka spectrum, use cases, responsibility aur evaluation ki jhalak.

Formula yaad kar lo: reasoning LLM + memory + tools + planning + reflection = AI agent. Baaki ki book isi formula ke har hisse ko ek-ek chapter me kholti hai.

01.1Part 1 — The Anatomy of an AI Agent

What is an AI Agent?

Classic definition: agent woh cheez hai jo apne environment ko sensors se perceive karti hai aur actuators se us par act karti hai — matlab agent sirf bolta nahi, dekhta hai → sochta hai → karta hai.

  • Environment = woh duniya jisse agent interact karta hai; user bhi environment ka hissa ho sakta hai.
  • Sensors = observe karne wale components — LLM agent ke liye text, image ya sound input.
  • Actuators = interact karne wale tools — calculator, search, code execution, file likhna.
  • Agent program ("brain") = observations se actions tak jaane ka logic; LLM-backed agent me ye ek reasoning LLM hota hai.

Example: user poochhta hai "5.1 × 7.3 kya hai?" — agent sunta hai (sensor), sochta hai ki calculation chahiye (brain), calculator tool chalata hai (actuator), result dekhta hai, phir jawab deta hai. Sirf text generate karna agent hona nahi hai; environment ke saath loop hona zaroori hai.

Ye definition classic AI textbook (2020, 4th edition) se aati hai — LLMs se bahut pehle ki hai, lekin aaj ke agents par bilkul fit baithti hai.

01.2Part 1 — The Anatomy of an AI Agent

LLMs — Agent ka Brain

LLM bas next token predict karta hai — input ko tokens me todta hai, ek-ek token generate karta hai, aur har baar apna output wapas input me daal deta hai. Isi loop ko autoregression kehte hain.

  • Tokenisation: "flamingos" jaise shabd tokens me tutte hain — jaise "flamingo" + "s". Model shabd nahi, tokens padhta aur likhta hai.
  • Autoregressive loop: ek token banao → use context me jodo → agla token banao. Har answer, har reasoning trace, har tool call isi loop se nikalta hai.
  • Matlab: model ke paas koi alag "sochne wala" hissa nahi hai — jo kuch bhi woh "sochta" hai, woh bhi tokens ke roop me hi generate hota hai. Ye baat Chapter 3 (reasoning) ki buniyaad hai.

Detail Chapter 2 me hai — tokens, training, Transformer, attention aur MoE, sab wahan khulega.

01.3Part 1 — The Anatomy of an AI Agent

Reasoning LLMs — System 1 vs System 2

Pehle progress train-time scaling se aayi — bada model, zyada data, zyada compute. Phir breakthrough aaya: reasoning LLMs jo jawab se pehle sochte hain.

  • Train-time scaling ki ceiling: model bada karne ka fayda kam hota gaya, cost badhti gayi.
  • Reasoning LLMs (jaise OpenAI o1, DeepSeek-R1): model pehle reasoning tokens generate karta hai — apne thoughts likhta hai — phir answer deta hai. Chat interfaces me ye thoughts aksar hidden ya summarised dikhte hain.
  • Psychology wali analogy: non-reasoning LLM ≈ System 1 (fast, intuitive, snap judgement); reasoning LLM ≈ System 2 (slow, deliberate, step-by-step).
  • Reasoning hi planning, tool selection aur reflection ko possible banata hai — lekin fast/cheap jawab chahiye to regular LLM behtar rehta hai.
  • Milestone: GPT-3.5 (original ChatGPT, Nov 2022) — woh model jisne sab kuch badal diya.

01.4Part 1 — The Anatomy of an AI Agent

Memory + Tools — Augmented LLM

LLM by default stateless hota hai — pichhli baat yaad nahi rehti. Memory aur tools judte hi woh augmented LLM ban jata hai — agent ka building block.

  • Stateless problem: multi-turn conversation me raw LLM pichhla sawaal bhool jata hai. Fix: conversation history ko prompt me wapas daal do.
  • Information overload: sab kuch daal dena bhi galat hai — isliye context engineering chahiye: kitni aur kaunsi info dein, iska balance.
  • Tools: LLM sirf text output kar sakta hai — jaise multiply(5.1, 7.3) likhna. Ye sirf intention hai, action nahi. Bahar ka software is text ko parse karke asli tool chalata hai.

Reasoning LLM + memory + tools — isi combination ko "augmented LLM" kaha gaya hai, aur yahi woh building block hai jise book agent me badalti hai.

01.5Part 1 — The Anatomy of an AI Agent

Planning & Reflection — Yahi Agent Banata Hai

Bade task ko chhote steps me todna, plan banana, execute karna, aur galti dikhe to reflect karke plan update karna — yahi loop agent ko autonomous banata hai.

  • Task decomposition: bada task → chhote, actionable steps. Jaise research task: pehle Google search, phir arXiv papers padhna.
  • Step-by-step execution: har step ke baad agent dobara sochta hai ki aage kya karna hai — plan fixed script nahi, live document hai.
  • Reflection: plan galat nikle to agent ruk kar sochta hai aur plan badalta hai — jaise Google + arXiv kaafi nahi lage to Semantic Scholar aur PubMed add kar dena.

Bina planning ke LLM ek-step wala jawab deta hai; planning + reflection ke saath woh goal ki taraf khud raasta banata hai. Chapter 6 me ReAct ke saath ye poora mechanism code me dikhega.

01.6Part 1 — The Anatomy of an AI Agent

Autonomy, Use Cases & Responsibility

Autonomy ek spectrum hai — ek step me tool choose karne se lekar poori freedom tak. Zyada agentic matlab zyada control, lekin zyada risk bhi.

Top use cases

  • Coding — sabse common. Goal clear hota hai, requirements defined hote hain, aur code automatically verify ho sakta hai (tests).
  • Deep research — arXiv / PubMed / Google Scholar se autonomous research.
  • Automation / standardisation — jaise hospitals ka scattered patient data structure karna. Lekin bina human ke patient diagnose karna — iske liye agent nahi.

Responsible use

  • Human-in-the-loop: output ya intermediate steps human check kare.
  • Guardrails: autonomy ko limit rakho — har kaam ke liye full freedom nahi.
  • Hallucination: LLM confidently galat bol sakta hai — checks zaroori hain.

Evaluation ki jhalak (Chapter 7)

  • Outcome — kaam hua ya nahi? Trajectory — kaise pahuncha, steps sahi aur efficient the?
  • Reliability (har baar succeed hota hai?) aur safety (malicious user? manipulated data? apni galti?) — alag-alag sawal hain.
  • Ek mashhoor persistent personal-assistant harness ne release ke kuch mahino me 300,000 GitHub stars liye — agents ab mainstream hain.

Harness ki duniya

  • Terminal-based: Claude Code, Gemini CLI, Codex CLI, OpenCode · Code-based: LangGraph, Smolagents, Pydantic AI · Hosted: Replit, v0, Manus · UI-based: Cursor, Windsurf, GitHub Copilot.
  • Sab ke peeche wahi scaffolding hai — LLM + memory + tools + planning — bas flavour alag hai.

Chapter 2 — Large Language Models

Har agent ke centre me ek LLM hai. Use samajhna matlab ye samajhna ki agent kya kar sakta hai aur kahan phas sakta hai — context limit, hallucination, tool-call format, ye sab LLM ki properties hain.

Is chapter me kya milega

  • 2.1 Tokens, autoregression, system prompt, multi-turn, tool calls ki pehli jhalak.
  • 2.2 Training — pre-training, SFT, RLHF, RLVR, GRPO.
  • 2.3 Transformer architecture — tokenizer, blocks, LM head, decoding, KV-cache.
  • 2.4 Self-attention deep dive — Q, K, V aur efficient attention (GQA, MLA, DSA).
  • 2.5 Mixture of Experts (MoE) — sparse vs active parameters, poori numbers table ke saath.

from dataclasses import dataclass

@dataclass
class Response:
    """Structured response from LLM calls."""

    content: str = ""
    reasoning: str | None = None
    tool_call: dict | None = None
    metadata: dict | None = None

# ------- next cell -------

import json
import urllib.request


class LLM:
    def __init__(
        self,
        model: str,
        base_url: str = "http://localhost:11434/v1",
        api_key: str = "no_key",
        think: bool = False,
        temperature: float | None = None,
    ):
        """Initialize the LLM with the given model."""
        self.model = model
        self.base_url = base_url
        self.api_key = api_key
        self.think = think
        self.temperature = temperature

    def generate(
        self, messages: list[dict], tools: list | None = None
    ) -> Response:
        """Generate a response from the LLM given a list of messages."""
        # Build the request body
        body = {
            "model": self.model,
            "messages": messages,
        }

        # Tools and Reasoning
        if tools:
            body["tools"] = tools
        if not self.think:
            body["reasoning_effort"] = "none"
        else:
            body["reasoning_effort"] = "medium"
        if self.temperature is not None:
            body["temperature"] = self.temperature

        # POST to the OpenAI-compatible /chat/completions endpoint
        request = urllib.request.Request(
            f"{self.base_url}/chat/completions",
            data=json.dumps(body).encode(),
            headers={
                "Content-Type": "application/json",
                "Authorization": f"Bearer {self.api_key}",
            },
        )
        with urllib.request.urlopen(request) as response:
            data = json.loads(response.read())

        # Extract message, tool_call, and metadata
        message = data["choices"][0]["message"]
        reasoning = message.get("reasoning") or message.get("reasoning_content")
        tool_calls = message.get("tool_calls")
        tool_call = tool_calls[0] if tool_calls else None
        metadata = {
            "model": data["model"],
            "prompt_tokens": data["usage"]["prompt_tokens"],
            "completion_tokens": data["usage"]["completion_tokens"],
        }

        # Format as Response dataclass
        return Response(
            content=message.get("content"),
            reasoning=reasoning,
            tool_call=tool_call,
            metadata=metadata,
        )

from dataclasses import dataclass

@dataclass
class Step:
    """A single step in an agent's trajectory."""

    thought: str = ""
    action: dict | None = None
    observation: str | None = None
    answer: str | None = None
    metadata: dict | None = None

# ------- next cell -------

class Trajectory:
    """Records agent execution as a sequence of runs."""
    def __init__(self) -> None:
        self.runs: list[dict] = []

    def initialize(self, query: str) -> None:
        """Register a new run with the given query."""
        self.runs.append({"query": query, "steps": []})

    def add(self, response: Response, observation: str | None = None) -> None:
        """Record a step from a Response, optionally with an observation."""
        # Add THOUGHT
        step = Step(
            thought=response.reasoning or "",
            metadata=response.metadata,
        )

        # Add ACTION/OBSERVATION or ANSWER
        if observation is not None:
            step.action = response.tool_call
            step.observation = observation
        else:
            step.answer = response.content
            
        self.runs[-1]["steps"].append(step)

# ------- next cell -------

from illustrated_agents.chapters.ch2 import trajectory_add_annotated; trajectory_add_annotated

# ------- next cell -------

class TinyAgent:
    """A minimal, modular, and educational agent framework."""

    def __init__(self, llm: LLM):
        self.llm = llm
        self.memory = None  # Chapter 4: Add Memory
        self.tools = None  # Chapter 5: Add Tools
        self.planner = None  # Chapter 6: Add Planning

        self.trajectory = Trajectory()

    def run(self, task: str) -> str:
        """Run the agent on a task."""
        self.trajectory.initialize(task)
        return self._step(task)

    def _step(self, task: str) -> str:
        """Perform a single step."""
        messages = [{"role": "user", "content": task}]
        response = self.llm.generate(messages)
        self.trajectory.add(response)
        return response.content

    def _execute_action(self, action: str) -> str | None:
        """Execute a tool action."""
        # Placeholder - will be implemented in later chapters
        return f"Executed action: {action}"

02.1Part 1 — The Anatomy of an AI Agent

Tokens, Prompts & Conversations

LLM ka input/output tokens hote hain — words, word-parts, numbers, punctuation. Model ek token generate karta hai, use input me jodta hai, agla banata hai — yahi autoregressive loop hai.

  • Tokenisation: "flamingos" → "flamingo" + "s". Token count hi cost aur context dono ko decide karta hai.
  • System prompt: deployer ka privileged instruction — user se pehle lagta hai, user ki baat se upar hota hai, aur bina model retrain kiye behaviour customise karta hai.
  • Multi-turn conversation: system / user / assistant roles se history track hoti hai — yahi Chapter 4 ki memory ki pehli seedhi hai.
  • Tool use ki pehli jhalak: LLM ek specific format me output karta hai (jaise structured web_search call), bahar ka wrapper use parse karke function chalata hai. Full detail Chapter 5 me.

Worked example: info-seeking agent — user ka sawaal → web search tool → retrieved info → jawab. Agent ka sabse simple roop yahi hai.

SOURCESource: An Illustrated Guide to AI Agents, O'Reilly, Chapter 2
← PichhlaChapter 2 — Large Language ModelsAgla →Training — Pre-training, SFT, RL
02.2Part 1 — The Anatomy of an AI Agent

Training — Pre-training, SFT, RL

Do phases: pre-training se base model banta hai, post-training (SFT + RL) se woh instruction-following model banta hai jo hum use karte hain.

  • Pre-training (language modeling): text ka span do, aakhri token chhupao, model se next word predict karwao; galat ho to loss se weights update karo — billions of times. Result: base model (sabse famous example: GPT-3, 2020). Data: curated web text, books, code.
  • SFT (supervised fine-tuning / instruction-tuning): prompt + desired completion ke pairs; prompt tokens loss se excluded hote hain, train sirf completion tokens par hota hai. Model instructions follow karna seekhta hai.
  • RLHF: human (ya reward-model) preference se train — do completions me se preferred ko upar, rejected ko neeche.
  • RLVR: reward automatically verifiable cheezon se — format sahi hai? final answer correct hai?
  • GRPO (Group Relative Policy Optimization): ek prompt ke liye group (jaise 5) responses generate karo, har ek ko reward do (example: format reward 0.3 + accuracy reward 0.7), group ke relative scores se update karo. Yahi algorithm Chapter 3 me DeepSeek-R1 ko train karta hai.
SOURCESource: An Illustrated Guide to AI Agents, O'Reilly, Chapter 2
← PichhlaTokens, Prompts & ConversationsAgla →Transformer Architecture & KV-Cache
02.3Part 1 — The Anatomy of an AI Agent

Transformer Architecture & KV-Cache

Transformer decoder ke 3 parts: tokenizer, Transformer blocks ka stack, aur LM head. Aur ek agent-developer ki sabse kaam ki cheez — KV-cache.

  • Tokenizer: text → token IDs; vocabulary jaise 50,000 tokens; har token ka ek embedding vector.
  • LM head: final vector ko poori vocabulary par probability distribution me badalta hai — wahi se next token chuna jata hai.
  • Decoding & temperature: temperature 0 = hamesha sabse probable token; temperature badhao = sampling, kam-probable tokens ko bhi chance. Creativity vs reliability ka yahi knob hai.
  • Context length: kitni "tracks" (tokens) ek saath process ho sakti hain — input ki limit. Yahi se context engineering paida hoti hai.
  • KV-cache (prompt/prefix caching): pehle pass ke baad previous tokens ke K/V reuse karo; har step sirf naya token process karo — speed aur cost dono behtar. Lambi agent trajectories ke liye cache optimise karna ek core skill hai.
  • Block ke andar: self-attention layer (context gather karta hai) + feed-forward network (representations process karta hai; factual associations yahin store hote hain — "The Shawshank" → "Redemption").
SOURCESource: An Illustrated Guide to AI Agents, O'Reilly, Chapter 2
← PichhlaTraining — Pre-training, SFT, RLAgla →Self-Attention Deep Dive — Q, K, V
02.4Part 1 — The Anatomy of an AI Agent

Self-Attention Deep Dive — Q, K, V

Self-attention do kaam karta hai: pehle relevance scoring (kaunsi purani info relevant hai), phir information combining (use current token me merge karna).

  • Q, K, V: 3 learned projection matrices input vectors ko queries (Q), keys (K) aur values (V) me badalti hain. Relevance = current token ki query × sab tokens ki keys; phir values ka weighted sum current token me merge hota hai. Formula: softmax(QKᵀ/√dₖ)V.
  • Example: "The dog chased the llama because it" — "it" kisko refer karta hai? Attention context se resolve karta hai.
  • Vanilla attention ki problem: har step par purane tokens ke K/V dobara compute hote — isliye KV-cache. Lekin cache memory khata hai, isliye efficient variants:
  • MHA — har head ke alag Q/K/V · GQA — heads K/V share karte hain · MQA — sab heads ek K/V share karte hain (kam accurate ho sakta hai).
  • MLA (Multi-head Latent Attention): K/V ko low-rank latent representation me compress karke cache karo; DeepSeek models se popular hua.
  • DSA (DeepSeek Sparse Attention): MLA ke upar Lightning Indexer + Top-K Selector — sirf top-K (paper me 2,048) tokens par attention.
  • RoPE (Rotary Position Embedding) position ki jaankari deta hai; FlashAttention is computation ko fast banata hai.
SOURCESource: An Illustrated Guide to AI Agents, O'Reilly, Chapter 2
← PichhlaTransformer Architecture & KV-CacheAgla →Mixture of Experts (MoE)
02.5Part 1 — The Anatomy of an AI Agent

Mixture of Experts (MoE)

Dense model me har token ke liye poora network active hota hai. MoE me uski jagah kai chhote experts hote hain — aur per token sirf kuch hi active hote hain. Isi liye bada model bhi fast inference deta hai.

  • Router / gate network har token ko decide karke 1–2 (ya zyada) experts ko bhejta hai.
  • Sparse parameters = saare parameters jo memory me load hain; active parameters = jo per token asal me chalte hain. Naming: Qwen3-30B-A3B = 30B sparse, 3B active.
  • Load balancing: ek expert dominate na kare — expert capacity (limit; overflow next-best expert ko), router me Gaussian noise, aur auxiliary loss (equal distribution par reward/punish).

from collections import Counter

# Self-consistency needs sampling diversity; we explicitly use temperature=1.
llm = LLM(model="gemma3:12b", temperature=1)

answers = []
for _ in range(10):
    query = """Six friends (Maarten, Ilse, Sarah, Jor, Irene, and Chris) are sitting in a row.

- Sarah is in seat 3.
- Chris is sitting at one of the ends of the row.
- Jor is sitting immediately to the right of Chris.
- Ilse is sitting exactly in the middle of Sarah and Maarten.
- Irene is not sitting next to Sarah.
- Maarten is sitting somewhere to the left of Irene.

In which seat is Maarten sitting?
Let's think step by step and give back your answer only after 'Answer:'.
"""

    # Generate response
    messages = [{"role": "user", "content": query},]
    response = llm.generate(messages)
    answer = response.content.split("Answer:")[-1].replace("\n", "").strip()
    answers.append(answer)

Counter(answers)

# ------- next cell -------

test_cases = [
    ("III", 3),
    ("IV", 4),
    ("IX", 9),
    ("LVIII", 58),
    ("MCMXCIV", 1994),
    ("MMMCMXCIX", 3999),
    ("", 0),
    ("IIII", 0),       # invalid: four in a row
    ("VV", 0),         # invalid: V can't repeat
    ("IC", 0),         # invalid: I can only subtract from V or X
    ("ABC", 0),        # invalid: non-Roman characters
    ("MMMM", 0),       # invalid: exceeds 3999
]


def verify(answer):
    try:
        # Extract the function
        namespace = {}
        exec(answer, namespace)
        fn = namespace["roman_to_int"]

        # Evaluate the function on test cases
        score = sum(fn(inp) == expected for inp, expected in test_cases) / len(test_cases)
        return score
    except Exception:
        # Return 0 if the code is not valid Python
        return 0.0

# ------- next cell -------

responses = []
for _ in range(10):
    # The query we want to ask the model
    query = """Write a Python function `roman_to_int(s)` that converts a Roman numeral 
string to an integer. The function should:
- Handle standard Roman numerals from 1 to 3999.
- Correctly handle subtractive notation (e.g., IV=4, IX=9, XL=40, XC=90, CD=400, CM=900).
- Return 0 for invalid inputs (empty string, non-Roman characters, or invalid patterns 
  like "IIII" or "VV").

Give only the function definition, no explanation or markdown formatting."""

    # Generate response
    response = llm.generate([{"role": "user", "content": query}])

    # Verify the response and compute a score
    score = verify(response.content)

    # Store the response and its score
    responses.append((response.content, score))

# Get highest score and the corresponding answer
best_answer, best_score = max(responses, key=lambda x: x[1])

# Show all scores
[response[1] for response in responses]

03.1Part 1 — The Anatomy of an AI Agent

System 1 vs System 2 & Test-Time Compute

Non-reasoning LLM seedha jawab deta hai; reasoning LLM pehle thinking tokens generate karta hai. Jitne zyada (aur meaningful) thinking tokens, utni behtar performance.

  • Train-time compute = pre-training + post-training par kharch (model size, data, FLOPs). Test-time compute = inference par kharch — zyada der sochna ya zyada answers generate karna.
  • Scaling laws: performance power law follow karta hai — compute double karo to fayda diminishing returns ke saath milta hai; log-log scale par straight line dikhti hai.
  • Kaplan scaling law: fixed budget me model size aur data ko balance karo. Chinchilla ne is balance ko refine kiya — model aur data dono saath badhao.
  • Evidence: test-time compute badhana ≈ train-time compute badhana, shayad usse aage bhi. Board-game experiments (AlphaZero + Hex) bhi yahi dikhate hain: fixed performance ke liye dono ka balance chahiye.

Isi liye 2024–25 me poora focus training se inference ki taraf shift hua — aur yahi agents ke liye sabse badi khabar hai, kyunki agent ka matlab hi hai inference par zyada compute kharch karna.

SOURCESource: An Illustrated Guide to AI Agents, O'Reilly, Chapter 3
← PichhlaChapter 3 — Reasoning Large Language ModelsAgla →Reward Models — ORM vs PRM
03.2Part 1 — The Anatomy of an AI Agent

Reward Models — ORM vs PRM

ORM sirf final answer ko judge karta hai; PRM reasoning ke har step ko score karta hai. Aksar dono ka mix behtar hota hai.

  • ORM (Outcome Reward Model): final answer sahi ya galat — reasoning steps ignore. Simple, lekin galat raaste se sahi jawab bhi pass ho jata hai.
  • PRM (Process Reward Model): har step ko score. Book ka flamingo riddle example (6 flamingos, 2 ude, 1 chhupa → 3 dikhte hain): step 2 me galti par low score, agle step me correction par high score.
  • Verifier LLM bhi ho sakta hai ya rule-based system (unit tests, compiler) — code ke liye rule-based verifier sabse bharosemand hai.

Poora chapter do categories me banta hai: search against verifiers (output-focused — sample karo, score karo, best chuno) aur modifying proposal distribution (input-focused — training/prompting se token probabilities badlo taaki reasoning tokens zyada chune jayein).

SOURCESource: An Illustrated Guide to AI Agents, O'Reilly, Chapter 3
← PichhlaSystem 1 vs System 2 & Test-Time ComputeAgla →Chain-of-Thought Prompting
03.3Part 1 — The Anatomy of an AI Agent

Chain-of-Thought Prompting

Non-reasoning LLM ke andar bhi reasoning chhupa hota hai — sahi prompt se bahar nikalo. Sabse mashhoor trick: prompt me bas jod do — "Let's think step by step".

  • Few-shot / one-shot: example reasoning dikhao. Book ka example: flamingo wale example ("6 − 2 = 4, phir 4 − 1 = 3") ke baad model penguin riddle ka sahi jawab 11 deta hai; concise-answer wale example se galat jawab 7 aaya tha!
  • Zero-shot CoT: bina example ke, sirf "Let's think step by step" — phir bhi sahi jawab (11 penguins).
  • Rule of thumb: zero-shot < one-shot < few-shot.
  • Sampling ke liye temperature 1 rakha jata hai (temperature 0 par har baar same output milega).
Yahi zero-shot CoT Chapter 6 me THOUGHT / ACTION fields ke roop me wapas aayega — ReAct ki neev yahin padti hai.
SOURCESource: An Illustrated Guide to AI Agents, O'Reilly, Chapter 3
← PichhlaReward Models — ORM vs PRMAgla →Self-Consistency & Best-of-N
03.4Part 1 — The Anatomy of an AI Agent

Self-Consistency & Best-of-N

3 steps: (1) multiple reasoning traces sample karo, (2) verifier/reward model score kare, (3) best answer chuno. Retrain karne ki zaroorat nahi — bas test-time compute badhao.

  • Self-consistency: verifier hi nahi — N answers sample karo aur majority vote lo. Book ka seating puzzle example: 6 friends, 10 samples → Counter({'5': 4, '1': 3, '4': 1, '2': 2}) — sabse common (5) hi sahi hai. Caveat: bahut mushkil tasks jahan model kabhi sahi hota hi nahi, wahan ye kaam nahi karta.
  • Best-of-N: ORM se answers score karo ya PRM se traces score karke average karo; weighted Best-of-N = PRM-weighted aggregation.
  • Worked example: roman_to_int function ko 12 test cases se verify karo (III=3 … MCMXCIV=1994; invalid IIII/VV/IC/ABC/MMMM → 0). 10 samples ke scores: [0.67, 0.58, 0.92, 0.92, 0.83, 0.75, 0.92, 0.92, 1.0, 0.25] — sirf ek perfect tha. Sampling + verifier = bina retrain ke behtar result.

Labs section me iska live version hai — khud samples chalao aur majority vote dekho.

SOURCESource: An Illustrated Guide to AI Agents, O'Reilly, Chapter 3
← PichhlaChain-of-Thought PromptingAgla →SFT se Reasoning — Flan & s1
03.5Part 1 — The Anatomy of an AI Agent

SFT se Reasoning — Flan & s1

Token distribution ko hi badal do taaki model reasoning tokens zyada chune. SFT se: query + reasoning trace + answer ke triplets par train karo.

  • Flan fine-tuning: 1,800+ tasks, CoT traces (arithmetic, multi-hop reasoning, NLI) mix karke ek bade model (540B parameters tak) ko fine-tune kiya gaya. Lekin reasoning data kam tha — poora reasoning model kehna jaldi hogi.
  • s1 — simple test-time scaling: sirf 1,000 questions + reasoning traces se ek 32B instruct model ko reasoning model bana diya! Special tokens se thinking aur answer alag rakhe jate hain.
  • Test-time control: thinking ko forcefully roko, ya "Wait" bolkar lamba karo — zyada thinking ≈ behtar performance. Matlab reasoning ki lambai bhi ek controllable knob hai.
SOURCESource: An Illustrated Guide to AI Agents, O'Reilly, Chapter 3
← PichhlaSelf-Consistency & Best-of-NAgla →DeepSeek-R1 — RL se Reasoning (5 Steps)
03.6Part 1 — The Anatomy of an AI Agent

DeepSeek-R1 — RL se Reasoning (5 Steps)

DeepSeek-R1-Zero ne dikhaya ki sirf RL (GRPO) se, bina SFT ke, model khud lambi reasoning seekh sakta hai. Phir DeepSeek-R1 ne usi ko 5 steps me production-quality banaya.

R1-Zero

  • Base model se start, koi SFT nahi, sirf RL (GRPO). System prompt me <think>…</think> aur <answer>…</answer> tags; do rule-based rewards — accuracy + format.
  • Model ne khud seekha: lambi reasoning → behtar answers.
  • Cold start problem: language mix karna (English + doosri language), kharab readability, formatting gayab.

R1 ke 5 steps

  1. Cold-start prevention: ~5,000 high-quality long-CoT samples par SFT.
  2. Reasoning-oriented RL (GRPO) + language-consistency reward — reasoning me strong, lekin non-reasoning tasks (translation/writing) me kamzor.
  3. Rejection sampling: reasoning data + non-reasoning data sample karke reward model se filter — 800,000 samples.
  4. SFT un 800k samples par base model ko — pehla asal R1.
  5. RL for all scenarios — helpfulness/harmlessness rewards + reasoning summarise karna → final DeepSeek-R1.

Pehle 3 steps asal me sirf synthetic data banane ke liye the — ye pattern (SFT → RL → data generation → SFT → RL) poori book me baar-baar dikhega.

Native reasoning: kuch open models me reasoning special tokens se ON/OFF hota hai — jaise ek model family me /think aur /no_think tokens (hybrid reasoning). Ollama chat templates ko automatically parse kar deta hai.
SOURCESource: An Illustrated Guide to AI Agents, O'Reilly, Chapter 3
← PichhlaSFT se Reasoning — Flan & s1Agla →Emerging Directions — Efficient & Latent Reasoning
03.7Part 1 — The Anatomy of an AI Agent

Emerging Directions — Efficient & Latent Reasoning

Lambi reasoning traces mehngi hain. Isliye teen naye raaste: multi-modal reasoning, efficient reasoning (chhoti traces), aur latent-space reasoning (mann me sochna, bina tokens likhe).

  • Multi-modal CoT (MCoT): 2-stage — pehle text+vision se rationale banao, phir rationale + original input se answer. Ek vision-CoT approach me 4 stages hain (summary, caption, reasoning, answer) aur 100,000 synthetic records se fine-tuning.
  • Chain-of-Draft (CoD): har reasoning step max 5 words ka draft — CoT jitni performance, bahut chhoti traces. Downside: users ke liye padhna mushkil.
  • Length rewards: short+correct ko zyada reward, long+wrong ko sabse kam. Kuch models "Think for 30 tokens" jaise explicit length control bhi seekhte hain.
  • Latent-space reasoning: CoT ko visible tokens ki jagah hidden representations me karo — last hidden state ko seedha next input banao, token decode skip karo. Ek approach me teacher (explicit CoT) se student (latent CoT) ko self-distillation se sikhaya jata hai.
  • Trade-off: latent reasoning efficient hai aur non-textual (symbolic/math) reasoning ki possibility deta hai — lekin reasoning dikhta nahi, isliye debugging mushkil ho jati hai.
SOURCESource: An Illustrated Guide to AI Agents, O'Reilly, Chapter 3
← PichhlaDeepSeek-R1 — RL se Reasoning (5 Steps)Agla →Chapter 4 — Memory
04Part 1 — The Anatomy of an AI Agent

Chapter 4 — Memory

LLM bhoolne wala (stateless) hai — memory hi use agent banati hai. Memory sirf conversation nahi: past actions, external knowledge, kya store karna hai aur kya bhoolna hai — ye sab memory design hai. Aakhir me context engineering — context window ko bharna nahi, curate karna hai.

Is chapter me kya milega

  • 4.1 Memory kyun — stateless LLMs aur memory ke 4 types.
  • 4.2 Short-term memory — conversation history, trimming, summarisation.
  • 4.3 Long-term memory — RAG aur embeddings.
  • 4.4 Agentic memory — MemoryBank, Agentic RAG, A-MEM, Search-o1.
  • 4.5 Context engineering — selection, reranking, MMR, lost-in-the-middle.

TinyAgent ko is chapter me Memory, TrimmingMemory, SummarizationMemory aur RAGMemory milte hain. Code chalane ke liye Ollama ke saath ek chhota embedding model bhi chahiye (book me 308M-parameter wala embedding model use hua hai).

class Memory:
    """Simple memory module to store conversation history."""

    def __init__(self):
        self.messages = []

    def add(
        self, role: str, content: str, tool_call: dict | None = None, **kwargs
    ) -> None:
        """Add a message to memory."""
        message = {"role": role, "content": content}

        # Tool call
        if tool_call:
            message["tool_calls"] = [tool_call]

        # Append message to memory
        self.messages.append(message)

    def get_messages(self) -> list[dict]:
        """Get all messages."""
        return self.messages

from illustrated_agents.chapters.ch2 import Trajectory

class TinyAgent:
    """A minimal, modular, and educational agent framework."""

    def __init__(self, llm: LLM, memory: Memory):
        self.llm = llm
        self.memory = memory
        self.tools = None  # Chapter 5: Add Tools
        self.planner = None  # Chapter 6: Add Planning

        self.trajectory = Trajectory()

    def run(self, task: str) -> str:
        """Run the agent on a task."""
        self.memory.add("user", task)
        self.trajectory.initialize(task)

        return self._step()

    def _step(self) -> str:
        """Perform a single step."""
        # Generate response and add to memory
        response = self.llm.generate(self.memory.get_messages())
        self.memory.add("assistant", response.content)
        self.trajectory.add(response)
        return response.content

    def _execute_action(self, action: str) -> str | None:
        """Execute a tool action."""
        # Placeholder - will be implemented in later chapters
        return f"Executed action: {action}"

import json
import urllib.request

class EmbeddingModel:
    """Generate embeddings."""

    def __init__(
        self,
        model: str,
        base_url: str = "http://localhost:11434/v1",
    ):
        """Initialize the embedding model with the given model."""
        self.model = model
        self.base_url = base_url

    def embed(self, text: str) -> list[float]:
        """Convert text into a numerical vector."""
        # POST to the OpenAI-compatible /embeddings endpoint
        request = urllib.request.Request(
            f"{self.base_url}/embeddings",
            data=json.dumps({"model": self.model, "input": text}).encode(),
            headers={"Content-Type": "application/json"},
        )
        with urllib.request.urlopen(request) as resp:
            response = json.loads(resp.read())

        # Extract and return the embedding
        return response["data"][0]["embedding"]

# ------- next cell -------

# Initialize EmbeddingGemma
embedding_model = EmbeddingModel(model="embeddinggemma")

# Test the embedding model
output = embedding_model.embed("Dolphins are amazing!")
output

from rich import print

# Create embeddings
embedding_a = embedding_model.embed("I love flamingos.")
embedding_b = embedding_model.embed("Dolphins use echolocation.")
embedding_c = embedding_model.embed("Flamingos are pink birds.")

# Calculate cosine similarity between A and B
dot_ab = sum(x * y for x, y in zip(embedding_a, embedding_b))
norm_a = sum(x * x for x in embedding_a) ** 0.5
norm_b = sum(x * x for x in embedding_b) ** 0.5
similarity_ab = dot_ab / (norm_a * norm_b)

# Calculate cosine similarity between A and C
dot_ac = sum(x * y for x, y in zip(embedding_a, embedding_c))
norm_c = sum(x * x for x in embedding_c) ** 0.5
similarity_ac = dot_ac / (norm_a * norm_c)

print(f"Similarity between [bold]'I love flamingos.'[/bold] and [bold]'Dolphins use echolocation.'[/bold]: {similarity_ab}")
print(f"Similarity between [bold]'I love flamingos.'[/bold] and [bold]'Flamingos are pink birds.'[/bold]: {similarity_ac}")

from illustrated_agents.chapters.ch4 import Memory

class RAGMemory(Memory):
    """Long-term Memory with RAG."""

    def __init__(self, embedding_model: EmbeddingModel, documents: list[str]):
        super().__init__()
        self.embedding_model = embedding_model
        self.documents = documents
        self.embeddings = [embedding_model.embed(doc) for doc in documents]

    def add(self, role: str, content: str, **kwargs) -> None:
        # Augment user queries with retrieved context before storing
        if role == "user":
            context = "\n".join(self.search(content))
            content = f"""Context:
{context}

Question: {content}"""
        super().add(role, content, **kwargs)

    def search(self, query: str) -> list[str]:
        """Return the top-k documents most similar to the query."""
        query_embed = self.embedding_model.embed(query)
        scores = [self._cosine(query_embed, embed) for embed in self.embeddings]
        ranked = sorted(range(len(scores)), key=lambda i: scores[i], reverse=True)
        return [self.documents[index] for index in ranked[:3]]

    def _cosine(self, a: list[float], b: list[float]) -> float:
        """Calculate cosine similarity between two embeddings.."""
        dot = sum(x * y for x, y in zip(a, b))
        norm = (sum(x * x for x in a) ** 0.5) * (sum(x * x for x in b) ** 0.5)
        return dot / norm

from illustrated_agents.chapters.ch4 import Memory

class TrimmingMemory(Memory):
    """Memory that keeps only the last two user/assistant turns."""

    def add(self, role: str, content: str, **kwargs) -> None:
        # Add the new message first using the parent class (Memory)
        super().add(role, content, **kwargs)

        # Then, keep system message plus the most recent two turns (4 messages)
        system = [message for message in self.messages if message["role"] == "system"]
        turns = [message for message in self.messages if message["role"] != "system"]
        self.messages = system + turns[-4:]

class SummarizationMemory(Memory):
    """Memory that compresses past turns into a running summary via an LLM."""

    def __init__(self, llm: LLM):
        super().__init__()
        self.llm = llm

    def add(self, role: str, content: str, **kwargs) -> None:
        # Add the new message first using the parent class (Memory)
        super().add(role, content, **kwargs)

        # After each completed turn, update the running summary
        if role == "assistant":
            # Split the existing summary from the new conversation turns
            summary = ""
            conversation = ""
            for message in self.messages:
                if message["role"] == "system":
                    summary = message["content"]
                else:
                    conversation += f"{message['role']}: {message['content']}\n"

            # Ask the LLM to extend the summary with the new conversation
            prompt = f"""Update the summary with the new conversation.

Summary: {summary}

Conversation:
{conversation}
Output the updated summary only."""
            response = self.llm.generate([{"role": "user", "content": prompt}])
            self.messages = [{"role": "system", "content": response.content}]

# ------- next cell -------

04.1Part 1 — The Anatomy of an AI Agent

Memory Kyun — 4 Types of Memory

Hosted chat products memory wale lagte hain kyunki unke peeche memory modules hain; raw LLM ko naam batao to bhi agle turn me bhool jata hai. Bina memory ke na personal assistant chalega, na coding agent, na planning.

  • Working (short-term): limited capacity, decision ke liye temporary info — LLM me = chat history jo har call me wapas di jati hai.
  • Episodic (long-term): specific events/experiences — agent ke liye uske past actions aur unke outcomes.
  • Semantic (long-term): duniya ka knowledge — agent ke liye Wikipedia/codebase jaise external databases.
  • Procedural (long-term): "kaise karna hai" — agent ke liye parameters me chhupa knowledge ya system prompt.
  • Parametric memory: model ke weights me pehle se stored knowledge. SFT se daalna possible hai lekin unstable — kya retain hoga, pakka nahi.

Memory = past actions + external info + nayi generated info. Bina memory ke tools aur planning dono impossible hain — agent ek hi action baar-baar dohrata rahega.

SOURCESource: An Illustrated Guide to AI Agents, O'Reilly, Chapter 4
← PichhlaChapter 4 — MemoryAgla →Short-Term Memory — Trimming & Summarisation
04.2Part 1 — The Anatomy of an AI Agent

Short-Term Memory — Trimming & Summarisation

Sabse basic memory: messages list har turn LLM ko wapas do. LLM "yaad" nahi karta — use prompt me bata diya jata hai. Lekin history badhti hai to context window bhar jata hai; isliye trimming aur summarisation.

  • Demo: "[Name] aur [Name] hain hum" → "Humare naam kya hain?" → model sahi jawab deta hai, kyunki history prompt me hai.
  • Context window problem: input + output tokens dono window me aate hain (book ka example: 8,192 me se 13 tokens used). History badhi to output cut hoga ya prompt hi process nahi hoga; zyada info se attention bhi bikharta hai.
  • Trimming: sirf aakhri 2 turns rakho (system + 4 messages) — simple, lekin purani important info kho sakti hai. TrimmingMemory yahi karta hai; demo me 4 questions ke baad sirf Q3–Q4 bachte hain.
  • Summarisation: har turn ke baad LLM se running summary update karwao (system message me store). Example: "[Name] — flamingos pink kyun?" ka summary — grey/white paida hote hain, carotenoids (shrimp, algae) se pink hote hain. Risk: baar-baar summarise karne se info compress hokar kho jati hai.
Debugging ke liye trajectory me raw history alag se track rakho — summary LLM ke liye hai, sach ka record raw history hai.
SOURCESource: An Illustrated Guide to AI Agents, O'Reilly, Chapter 4
← PichhlaMemory Kyun — 4 Types of MemoryAgla →Long-Term Memory — RAG & Embeddings
04.3Part 1 — The Anatomy of an AI Agent

Long-Term Memory — RAG & Embeddings

Long-term memory = external database jo query ki ja sakti hai. Sabse common tareeka: RAG (Retrieval-Augmented Generation) — fayda: hallucination kam, kyunki model ko sachchi external info milti hai.

RAG ke 2 hisse

  • Ingestion: external text → embedding model se numerical vectors (embeddings) → vector database.
  • Inference — 4 steps: (1) query embed karo, (2) database se most relevant docs nikalo (similarity se), (3) docs + query ko prompt me jodo, (4) LLM answer generate kare.

Embeddings hands-on

  • Book ka embedding model: 308M parameters, har text ke 768 values (har value −1…1 ke beech).
  • Cosine similarity = dot product / (lengths ka product); chhota angle = zyada similar.
  • Example numbers: "I love flamingos" vs "Dolphins use echolocation" = 0.355; vs "Flamingos are pink birds" = 0.639. Dusra pair zyada similar hai — aur numbers bhi yahi kehte hain.
  • RAGMemory ke steps: docs embed karo → query embed karo → similarity → top docs → prompt me add karo.

Labs me RAG simulator hai — query badlo, top-k ghumao, dekho kaunse docs retrieve hote hain.

SOURCESource: An Illustrated Guide to AI Agents, O'Reilly, Chapter 4
← PichhlaShort-Term Memory — Trimming & SummarisationAgla →Agentic Memory — MemoryBank, A-MEM, Search-o1
04.4Part 1 — The Anatomy of an AI Agent

Agentic Memory — MemoryBank, A-MEM, Search-o1

Memory ko agent khud manage kare to naye patterns nikalte hain — bhoolna bhi ek feature hai, aur retrieval ko reasoning ke beech me bhi use kiya ja sakta hai.

  • MemoryBank: chatbot ke liye long-term memory — past events ke summaries + user portrait. Forgetting curve se inspired: jo memory retrieve hoti rehti hai woh reinforce hoti hai, jo nahi hoti woh fade ho jati hai (spaced repetition jaisa).
  • Agentic RAG: RAG me agent khud retrieval ko control kare — ek agent multiple processes sambhale, ya multiple agents alag processes; reasoning ke dauraan bhi RAG use ho sakta hai.
  • A-MEM: Zettelkasten note-taking se inspired — har note atomic (ek hi subject) aur linked. Nayi memory aane par purani memories se link banta hai — evolutionary approach.
  • Search-o1: reasoning ke beech search karo, context ko LLM se compress karwao, phir reasoning continue karo.
SOURCESource: An Illustrated Guide to AI Agents, O'Reilly, Chapter 4
← PichhlaLong-Term Memory — RAG & EmbeddingsAgla →Context Engineering — The Frontier
04.5Part 1 — The Anatomy of an AI Agent

Context Engineering — The Frontier

Context window bade ho gaye hain, lekin "bada window = sab daal do" galat hai. Context engineering = sahi info, sahi jagah, sahi matra me.

  • Pipeline: context tracking & storage (kya track karein — agent behaviour: tool usage/outputs, reasoning steps, failures/successes; user behaviour: intent, feedback, approvals; knowledge: DB snapshots, artifacts; system: policies/guardrails) → selection → compression.
  • Reranking: retrieved docs ko query-relevance se dobara rank karo, sirf top rakho — deep research me bahut useful.
  • MMR (Maximal Marginal Relevance): relevance + diversity dono. Ek jaisi docs ki bheed nahi, varied docs chuno — relevance vector (query se similarity) aur redundancy matrix (docs aapas me kitne similar) se faisla hota hai.
  • Lost-in-the-middle: lambi context me beech ki info model bhool jata hai — important info shuru ya end me rakho.
  • Needle-in-a-haystack test: bade document me specific info dhoondhne ki capability ka test.
  • Multi-agent context engineering: har agent ko sirf uska relevant context do — isolation bhi ek technique hai (Chapter 8).
SOURCESource: An Illustrated Guide to AI Agents, O'Reilly, Chapter 4

05Part 1 — The Anatomy of an AI Agent

Chapter 5 — Tool Usage, Learning, and Protocols

LLM sirf text nikaal sakta hai — tools hi use duniya se jodte hain. Tool use ke 5 steps, tools sikhane ke 3 tareeke (prompting, SFT, RL), aur standardisation: MCP (tools ke liye) aur Skills (procedural knowledge ke liye).

Is chapter me kya milega

  • 5.1 Tool usage ke 5 steps — creation → definition → selection → calling → output processing.
  • 5.2 Tool learning — in-context learning, SFT (Toolformer), RL (ToolRL, Search-R1).
  • 5.3 Native tool calling — model khud structured tool calls deta hai.
  • 5.4 MCP — "AI ka USB-C port", N×M problem ka jawab.
  • 5.5 Skills — tools batate hain agent kya kar sakta hai; Skills batate hain kaise.

TinyAgent ko Tools / NativeTools aur toolbox.py milte hain. Ek mashhoor gotcha: SummarizationMemory Tools ko tod deta hai, kyunki woh us system prompt ko overwrite kar deta hai jisme tool definitions hain — fix: system prompt ko replace karne ke bajaye uska ek section update karo.

import random

def get_weather(location: str) -> str:
    temperature = random.randint(10, 30)

from typing import Callable

class Tools:
    """Tool registry for the Agent."""

    def __init__(self, requires_approval: list[str] = []):
        """Initialize and select tools that require approval before execution.
        """
        self.registry = {}
        self.requires_approval = requires_approval

    def add_tool(self, name: str, func: Callable, description: str):
        """Register a tool that the Agent can use.

        Arguments:
            name: The name of the tool.
            func: The function implementing the tool.
            description: A description of the tool.
        """
        self.registry[name] = {"function": func, "description": description}

    @property
    def schemas(self):
        """Used only for native tool-calling."""
        return None

class Tools:
    """Tool registry for the Agent."""

    def __init__(self, requires_approval: list[str] = []):
        """Initialize and select tools that require approval before execution.
        """
        self.registry = {}
        self.requires_approval = requires_approval

        """Register a tool that the Agent can use.

        Arguments:
            name: The name of the tool.
            func: The function implementing the tool.
            description: A description of the tool.

    @property

        """Used only for native tool-calling."""

        """Get descriptions of all registered tools."""
        return "\n".join(
            f"`{tool}`: {self.registry[tool]['description']}" for tool in self.registry

    def prompt(self):

{self.descriptions}

To use a tool, respond with JSON: {{"tool": "name", "kwargs": {{"param": "value"}}}}
"""

    def parse(self, response: Response) -> Response:
        """Parse a JSON tool call from text."""
        text = response.content

        if '"tool":' in text or '"tool:"' in text:
            start, end = text.find("{"), text.rfind("}") + 1
            tool_call = json.loads(text[start:end])

            # Add the parsed tool call to the response
            return Response(
                content=response.content,
                reasoning=response.reasoning,
                tool_call=tool_call,
            )

        return response

    def execute(self, response: Response) -> Any:
        """Run a registered tool.

        Arguments:
            tool_call: A parsed tool call dict with "tool" and "kwargs" keys.
        """
        tool_call = response.tool_call
        name, kwargs = tool_call["tool"], tool_call.get("kwargs", {})

        # Human-in-the-loop: ask before running dangerous tools
        if name in self.registry and name in self.requires_approval:
            response = input(f"Allow {name}? [y/N] ").strip().lower()
            if response not in ("y", "yes"):
                return f"Tool '{name}' was denied by the user."

        # Handle registered tools
        if name in self.registry:
            tool_func = self.registry[name]["function"]
            return tool_func(**kwargs)

        return f"Tool '{name}' not found."

    def observation(self, result):
        """Return the observation as a user."""
        return "user", f"OBSERVATION: {result}"

    def is_done(self, response: Response) -> bool:
        """The `TinyAgent` is done if there is no tool call, 
        or if it uses the `final_answer` tool."""
        if not response.tool_call:
            return True
        if response.tool_call["tool"] == "final_answer":
            response.content = response.tool_call.get("kwargs", "")
            return True
        return False

    @property
    def schemas(self):
        """Used only for native tool-calling."""
        return None

from illustrated_agents.chapters.ch2 import Trajectory
from illustrated_agents.chapters.ch4 import Memory


class TinyAgent:
    """A minimal, modular, and educational agent framework."""

    def __init__(self, llm: LLM, memory: Memory, tools: Tools):
        self.llm = llm
        self.memory = memory
        self.tools = tools
        self.planner = None  # Chapter 6: Add Planning

        self.trajectory = Trajectory()

        # Build system prompt with all components
        system_prompt = "You are a helpful assistant.\n\n"
        system_prompt += self.tools.prompt
        self.memory.add("system", system_prompt)

    def run(self, task: str) -> str:
        """Run the agent on a task."""
        self.memory.add("user", task)
        self.trajectory.initialize(task)

        return self._step()

    def _step(self) -> str:
        """Perform a single step."""
        # THOUGHT: Generate response and add to memory
        response = self.llm.generate(self.memory.get_messages(), tools=self.tools.schemas)
        self.memory.add("assistant", response.content, tool_call=response.tool_call)

        # Tool parsing
        response = self.tools.parse(response)

        # ANSWER: Stopping mechanism
        if self.tools.is_done(response):
            self.trajectory.add(response)
            return response.content

        return self._execute_action(response)

    def _execute_action(self, response: Response) -> None:
        """Execute a tool action."""

        # ACTION: execute tools
        result = self.tools.execute(response)

        # OBSERVATION: add tool results to memory and display
        role, observation = self.tools.observation(result)
        self.memory.add(role, observation)
        self.trajectory.add(response, observation)

        return observation

import sys
from mcp.client.stdio import stdio_client, StdioServerParameters
from mcp import ClientSession


async def list_tools():
    # The parameters to start the MCP server
    server_params = StdioServerParameters(command=sys.executable, args=[SERVER_PATH])
    
    # Connect to the MCP server over stdio
    async with stdio_client(server_params, errlog=None) as (read, write):
        async with ClientSession(read, write) as session:
            await session.initialize()
            
            tools = await session.list_tools()
            for tool in tools.tools:
                print(f"Name: {tool.name}")
                print(f"Description: {tool.description}")
                print(f"Parameters: {tool.input_schema}")
                print()

await list_tools()

# ------- next cell -------

async def call_tool():
    # The parameters to start the MCP server
    server_params = StdioServerParameters(
        command=sys.executable,
        args=[SERVER_PATH],
    )
    
    # Connect to the MCP server over stdio
    async with stdio_client(server_params, errlog=None) as (read, write):
        async with ClientSession(read, write) as session:
            await session.initialize()
            
            result = await session.call_tool("read_markdown", {"path": "https://raw.githubusercontent.com/MaartenGr/BERTopic/refs/heads/master/README.md"})
            print(result.content[0].text)

await call_tool()

import asyncio

from illustrated_agents.tools import Tools

class MCPTools(Tools):
    """MCP-based tool registry that extends Tools."""

    def __init__(self):
        super().__init__()
        self._load_mcp_tools()

    def _get_server_params(self):
        return StdioServerParameters(command=sys.executable, args=[SERVER_PATH])

    def _load_mcp_tools(self):
        """Fetch tools from MCP server and register them."""

        # Fetch the list of tools from the MCP server
        async def fetch():
            async with stdio_client(self._get_server_params(), errlog=None) as (read, write):
                async with ClientSession(read, write) as session:
                    await session.initialize()
                    tools = await session.list_tools()
                    return tools.tools

        mcp_tools = asyncio.run(fetch())

        # Register each MCP tool using parent's add_tool
        for tool in mcp_tools:
            self.add_tool(
                name=tool.name,
                func=self._make_tool_caller(tool.name),
                description=tool.description,
            )

    def _make_tool_caller(self, name: str):
        """Create a callable that invokes the MCP tool."""

        def caller(**kwargs):
            return asyncio.run(self._call_tool(name, kwargs))

        return caller

    async def _call_tool(self, name: str, args: dict) -> str:
        """Call a tool on the MCP server."""
        async with stdio_client(self._get_server_params(), errlog=None) as (read, write):
            async with ClientSession(read, write) as session:
                await session.initialize()
                result = await session.call_tool(name, args)
                return result.content[0].text

import inspect
from typing import Callable

# Convert specific types to string descriptions
TYPE_MAP = {
    str: "string", int: "integer", float: "number", 
    bool: "boolean", list: "array", dict: "object"
}

def tool_to_schema(function: Callable) -> dict:
    """Convert a Python function to an OpenAI-style tool schema."""
    signature = inspect.signature(function)

    # Extract meatadata
    properties, required = {}, []
    for name, parameter in signature.parameters.items():
        properties[name] = {"type": TYPE_MAP.get(parameter.annotation, "string")}
        if parameter.default is inspect.Parameter.empty:
            required.append(name)

    # Fill schema
    schema = {
        "type": "function",
        "function": {
            "name": function.__name__,
            "description": inspect.getdoc(function),
            "parameters": {
                "type": "object",
                "properties": properties,
                "required": required,
            },
        },
    }

    return schema

# ------- next cell -------

import json
from illustrated_agents.chapters.ch2 import Response
from illustrated_agents.chapters.ch5 import Tools


class NativeTools(Tools):
    """Tool registry using native function calling."""

    @property
    def schemas(self) -> list[dict]:
        """Return tool functions for native function calling."""
        return [
            tool_to_schema(tool["function"]) for tool in self.registry.values()
        ]

    @property
    def prompt(self) -> str:
        """Empty because we don't need a prompt for native tool calling"""
        return ""

    def parse(self, response: Response) -> Response:
        """Parse a tool call."""
        # If there's no tool call, return the response as is
        if not response.tool_call:
            return response

        # Extract the tool name and arguments from the tool call
        args = response.tool_call["function"]["arguments"]
        if isinstance(args, str):
            args = json.loads(args)
        tool_call = {
            "tool": response.tool_call["function"]["name"],
            "kwargs": args,
        }

        # Add the parsed tool call to the response
        return Response(
            content=response.content,
            reasoning=response.reasoning,
            tool_call=tool_call,
        )

    def observation(self, result: str) -> tuple[str, str]:
        """Native tool results use the 'tool' role."""
        return "tool", str(result)

    def is_done(self, response: Response) -> bool:
        """No tool call means the `TinyAgent` is done."""
        return not response.tool_call

import inspect
import yaml
from pathlib import Path
from illustrated_agents.chapters.ch5 import NativeTools

class Skills(NativeTools):
    """A `Tools` and `Skills` registry

    Skills are recipes. When you activate one, you get instructions
    in return on how to approach a given task. Although it is not
    a tool in the same way a calculator is one, we can still approach
    it as such since the Agent has to decide when to activate it.

    The skills are loaded progressively. As such, the name and description are
    available in the system prompt, but the full instructions are only injected
    when the agent **activates** a skill (uses it as a tool).
    """

    def add_skill(self, path: str):
        """Load a SKILL.md from a skill folder and register it as a tool."""
        skill_dir = Path(path)
        content = (skill_dir / "SKILL.md").read_text(encoding="utf-8")
        
        # TIER 2: Instructions - Full instructions of the main SKILL.md
        _, frontmatter, instructions = content.split("---", 2)
        meta = yaml.safe_load(frontmatter)

        # TIER 1: Catalog - Name and description of a skill
        name, description = meta["name"], meta["description"]
        
        # TIER 3: List files in the same folder that the agent can access
        extra_files = [p.name for p in skill_dir.iterdir() if p.name != "SKILL.md"]
        
        # When activated, return the instructions plus the folder context
        def skill(**kwargs):
            return f"""{instructions}

Skill folder: {skill_dir}

Available files: {extra_files}"""
        
        skill.__name__ = name
        skill.__doc__ = "A skill. " + description
        skill.__signature__ = inspect.Signature()
        self.add_tool(name, skill, "A skill. " + description)

    @property
    def prompt(self):
        return """You have specialized skills available.
To activate a skill, call it with an empty argument object.
Skills return instructions; they do not process the task directly."""

SOURCESource: An Illustrated Guide to AI Agents, O'Reilly, Chapter 5
← PichhlaContext Engineering — The FrontierAgla →Tool Usage ke 5 Steps
05.1Part 1 — The Anatomy of an AI Agent

Tool Usage ke 5 Steps

Tools do kaam karte hain: action lena (kuch badalna) ya information retrieve karna. Aur har tool call ek fixed 5-step pipeline se guzarta hai.

  1. Tool creation: function banao — jaise multiply(a: str, b: str) -> float (LLM sirf text deta hai, isliye strings lo, float me convert karo). Registry dict me save karo. Docstrings critical hain — LLM unhi se tool samajhta hai.
  2. Tool definition: LLM ko batao tools kya hain, kya karte hain, kab use karein — natural language (system prompt) ya structured JSON Schema (name, description, parameters, required). Best practices: tools extensively document karo; sankhya kam rakho (10 se kam se start karo); har tool ka scope chhota rakho.
  3. Tool selection: sahi tool chunna — reasoning LLM yahan chamakta hai. Zyada tools hon to RAG se tool discovery: tool schemas vector DB me, query se relevant nikalo.
  4. Tool calling: LLM output string me tool call banata hai — ye sirf intention hai. Bahar ka code parse karke execute karta hai (Tools.parse() / .execute()); dangerous tools ke liye requires_approval — human-in-the-loop.
  5. Output processing: tool ka output wapas LLM ko do — messages me user role se, OBSERVATION: prefix ke saath, taaki LLM agla step decide kar sake.

Demo: "What is 5.1 times 7.3?" → tool call → OBSERVATION: 37.23. Labs me is poori pipeline ka live simulator hai.

SOURCESource: An Illustrated Guide to AI Agents, O'Reilly, Chapter 5
← PichhlaChapter 5 — Tool Usage, Learning, and ProtocolsAgla →Tool Learning — Prompting, SFT, RL
05.2Part 1 — The Anatomy of an AI Agent

Tool Learning — Prompting, SFT, RL

Tool use sikhane ke 3 tareeke: prompt me example do, SFT se mimic karwao, ya RL se khud seekhne do. Teeno ka trade-off alag hai.

  • (a) In-context learning / few-shot prompting: prompt me examples do — LLM pattern follow karta hai; messages me aisa dikhao jaise model pehle hi tools use kar chuka hai. Koi fine-tuning nahi; capable model par behtar kaam karta hai.
  • (b) SFT — Toolformer: model khud decide kare kab API call karni hai. Special tokens: [ = tool call shuru, → = execute karo, ] = output mil gaya. Example: "5.1 * 7.3 is [Calculator(5.1*7.3)→37.23] The answer is 37.23." Limitations: SFT mimic karta hai — exact wording par sensitive; ek kaam ke kai sahi tool calls ho sakte hain; training data assume karta hai tools kabhi fail nahi hote — real life me hote hain.
  • (c) RL — Tool-Integrated Reasoning (TIR): tools ko reasoning trace ke andar call karo, reasoning continue karo. ToolRL: GRPO ke saath 2 rewards — correctness (sahi tool + parameters?) aur format. 4,000 TIR traces par training. Note: lambi reasoning traces se tool tasks me fayda nahi, chhote models ko nuksaan bhi.
  • Search-R1: search ko tool banakar reasoning me interleave karo — <think> → <search> → <information> → <answer>; search output tokens loss me masked rehte hain.
SOURCESource: An Illustrated Guide to AI Agents, O'Reilly, Chapter 5
← PichhlaTool Usage ke 5 StepsAgla →Native Tool Calling
05.3Part 1 — The Anatomy of an AI Agent

Native Tool Calling

Prompt-based calling "magical" nahi hai — pehle khud karke samjho, phir native use karo. Native me LLM khud structured tool_calls deta hai; koi text parsing nahi.

  • NativeTools class JSON Schema banata hai aur output parse karta hai; tool ka result alag tool role se wapas jata hai.
  • Modern open models ke chat templates me tool declaration ke liye special tokens hote hain — model ko training se hi ye format aata hai.
  • Native + reasoning dono hon to Chapter 6 ka ReAct bina prompt-parsing ke chalta hai — model ka reasoning hi THOUGHT hai, tool call hi ACTION.
Book ki pedagogy: pehle prompt-based tareeke se har step haath se karo taaki mechanism samajh aaye, phir native par move karo. SPA ke labs me bhi yahi order rakha gaya hai.
SOURCESource: An Illustrated Guide to AI Agents, O'Reilly, Chapter 5
← PichhlaTool Learning — Prompting, SFT, RLAgla →MCP — Model Context Protocol
05.4Part 1 — The Anatomy of an AI Agent

MCP — Model Context Protocol

Problem: N × M — N LLMs × M tools = har combination ke liye custom integration. MCP (Nov 2024, open standard) ek hi standard connection deta hai: N + M connections.

3 core components

  • MCP host — LLM application (Cursor, ChatGPT, Claude, GitHub Copilot); connections manage aur routing karta hai.
  • MCP client — host ke andar; ek server se one-to-one connection, discovery + forwarding.
  • MCP server — lightweight program jo tools/context expose karta hai (jaise arXiv server). 3 primitives: tools (actions), resources (context data — files, documents), prompts (reusable templates).

Flow (12 steps, short me)

User: "Summarize the 5 latest commits" → host → client server se tools poochhta hai (/list_commits, /create_pr…) → LLM ko prompt + tools → LLM /list_commits chunta hai → client → server execute karta hai → output wapas → LLM summarise karta hai → user ko answer. Communication: JSON-RPC 2.0. API badle to fix ek jagah (tool provider ke server par) hota hai.

Confusion door karo: MCP tools ke liye hai, A2A (Chapter 8) agents ke beech baat ke liye — dono alag layers hain. Repo me MCP ko TinyAgent me daalne ka ek extra notebook bhi hai (core flow se alag).
SOURCESource: An Illustrated Guide to AI Agents, O'Reilly, Chapter 5

05.5Part 1 — The Anatomy of an AI Agent

Skills — Procedural Knowledge

Tools batate hain agent kya kar sakta hai; Skills batate hain kaise — recurring task ka recipe: steps, conventions, references. Har baar dobara batane ki zaroorat nahi.

Progressive disclosure — 3 layers

LayerKab load hoti haiKya hota haiSize
1Hamesha loadedSKILL.md metadata (YAML: name + description)~100 tokens
2Skill activate hone parSKILL.md instructions (Markdown)<5,000 tokens
3Zaroorat padne parBundled resources (scripts, reference files)Jitna chahiye
  • Example: meeting_notes/ skill — SKILL.md + scripts/extract_action_items.py + formats/ (one-on-one, team meeting, external call ke alag formats).
  • Example convention: "presentation banao: web search → summarise → slides ek-ek karke" ya "uv use karo, pip nahi" — ek baar likho, har baar apply.
  • Fayda: context window lean rehta hai — skill tabhi load hoti hai jab relevant ho. Ye Chapter 4 ke context engineering ka hi ek roop hai.

06Part 1 — The Anatomy of an AI Agent

Chapter 6 — Planning and Reflection

Planning + reflection hi LLM ko agent banate hain — ye single agent ka aakhri core component hai. Plan banao, actions ko sequence me chalao (ReAct), phir reflect karke improve karo.

Is chapter me kya milega

  • 6.1 Task decomposition aur planning prompts — CoT, Least-to-Most, Plan-and-Solve.
  • 6.2 Action sequencing — ReAct: THOUGHT / ACTION / OBSERVATION ka loop.
  • 6.3 Reflection — Self-Refine, Reflexion, CRITIC.
  • 6.4 Agents jo khud improve hote hain — TTRL aur R-Zero.

Is chapter ke end me TinyAgent ko ReAct planner milta hai aur run() ek for-loop ban jata hai — book ke shabdon me, agent ki autonomy aakhir me "iteratively calling an LLM until it decides to stop" par hi tikti hai. TinyAgent ki true foundation yahin complete hoti hai.

import re
from illustrated_agents.chapters.ch2 import Response

class ReAct:
    """ReAct module."""

    def __init__(self, max_steps: int = 10):
        """Initialize ReAct module.

        Arguments:
            max_steps: Maximum number of ReAct steps to perform.
        """
        self.max_steps = max_steps

    @property
    def prompt(self) -> str:
        return """
# ReAct (Reason and Act)

You are a ReAct agent that performs exactly ONE step per turn.

## ReAct Format

You use the following format for each step:

THOUGHT: [Your reasoning about what to do next]
ACTION:
{
    "tool": "a_tool_name",
    "kwargs": {"param": "value"},
}

An observation will be provided after each action. You do not generate the observation yourself.

## ReAct Completion

To provide the final answer to the task, use an action blob with "tool": "final_answer" tool. 
It is the only way to complete the task, else you will be stuck on a loop. 
So your final output should look like this:

ACTION:
{
    "tool": "final_answer",
    "kwargs": "insert your final answer here"
}

Use the `final_answer` tool when you are completely done with all subtasks and have the final answer ready.
You can also use `final_answer` to directly reply to a user's question without using any other tools.

"""

    def parse(self, response: Response) -> Response:
        """Parse a ReAct formatted response into THOUGHT and ACTION."""
        text = response.content

        # The patterns for each section
        patterns = {
            "THOUGHT": r"THOUGHT:\s*(.+?)(?=ACTION:|OBSERVATION:|$)",
            "ACTION": r"ACTION:\s*(.+?)(?=THOUGHT:|OBSERVATION:|$)",
        }

        # Extract each section using regex
        result = {}
        for key, pattern in patterns.items():
            match = re.search(pattern, text, re.DOTALL)
            result[key] = match.group(1).strip() if match else ""

        # Update Response and extract only the action
        response.content = result["ACTION"]
        response.reasoning = result["THOUGHT"]
        return response

from illustrated_agents.chapters.ch2 import Response, Trajectory
from illustrated_agents.chapters.ch4 import Memory
from illustrated_agents.chapters.ch5 import Tools


class TinyAgent:
    """A minimal, modular, and educational agent framework."""

    def __init__(self, llm: LLM, memory: Memory, tools: Tools, planner: ReAct):
        self.llm = llm
        self.memory = memory
        self.tools = tools
        self.planner = planner

        self.trajectory = Trajectory()

        # Build system prompt with all components
        system_prompt = "You are a helpful assistant.\n\n"
        system_prompt += self.planner.prompt
        system_prompt += self.tools.prompt
        self.memory.add("system", system_prompt)

    def run(self, task: str) -> str:
        """Run the agent on a task."""
        self.memory.add("user", task)
        self.trajectory.initialize(task)

        # *Autonomy* loop
        for step in range(self.planner.max_steps):
            result = self._step()
            if result is not None:
                return result

    def _step(self) -> str | None:
        """Perform a single step."""
        # THOUGHT: Generate response and add to memory
        response = self.llm.generate(
            self.memory.get_messages(), tools=self.tools.schemas
        )
        self.memory.add(
            "assistant", response.content, tool_call=response.tool_call
        )

        # Tool parsing
        response = self.planner.parse(response)
        response = self.tools.parse(response)

        # ANSWER: Stopping mechanism
        if self.tools.is_done(response):
            self.trajectory.add(response)
            return response.content

        return self._execute_action(response)

    def _execute_action(self, response: Response) -> None:
        """Execute a tool action."""

        # ACTION: execute tools
        result = self.tools.execute(response)

        # OBSERVATION: add tool results to memory and display
        role, observation = self.tools.observation(result)
        self.memory.add(role, observation)
        self.trajectory.add(response, observation)

        return None

06.1Part 1 — The Anatomy of an AI Agent

Task Decomposition & Planning Prompts

Bina plan ke agent ko pata hi nahi aage kya karna hai. Plan malleable hona chahiye — bug mile to implement + test dobara loop me aate hain.

  • Example plan (feature banana): (1) requirements clarify, (2) codebase analyse, (3) design, (4) implement, (5) test, (6) docs update. Har (sub)task ke saath tool bhi likha ho sakta hai — jaise analyse ke liye code-retrieval tool.
  • CoT as planning: "Let's think step-by-step" se model pehle steps sochta hai, phir plan banata hai — CoT ka thinking hi planning hai.
  • Self-consistency / Tree of Thoughts: multiple CoT traces sample karo, best chuno. Tree of Thoughts me har node ek "thought"/subtask — Beam Search / Monte Carlo Tree Search + reward models se best path.
  • Least-to-Most: pehle problem ko subproblems me todo, phir ek-ek solve karo — har subproblem ka solution agle prompt me feed hota hai.
  • Plan-and-Solve: zero-shot — "pehle plan banao, phir step-by-step solve karo" + answer extraction.

Aaj ke LLMs zyada tar bina complex prompts ke plan bana lete hain — lekin uske liye training me CoT/planning traces chahiye hote hain.

SOURCESource: An Illustrated Guide to AI Agents, O'Reilly, Chapter 6
← PichhlaChapter 6 — Planning and ReflectionAgla →ReAct — Reason + Act
06.2Part 1 — The Anatomy of an AI Agent

ReAct — Reason + Act

Pehle reasoning aur acting alag-alag the; ReAct dono ko interleave karta hai: har loop me THOUGHT → ACTION → OBSERVATION → dobara THOUGHT… jab tak kaam poora na ho.

TinyAgent ka ReAct

  • ReAct class: max_steps=10; final_answer tool hi finish karne ka ekmatra tareeka hai; parser regex se THOUGHT/ACTION alag karta hai.
  • TinyAgent.run() me for-loop — yahi autonomy hai.
  • Demo: (4.6 + 6.685) × 4 − 3.14 → 4 steps: add → 11.285, multiply → 45.14, subtract → 42.0, final_answer → 42.0. Labs me iska step-by-step simulator hai.

Native ReAct

  • Reasoning + native tool calling wale model par prompt/parse ki zaroorat nahi — prompt empty, parse identity. Model ka reasoning = THOUGHT, tool call = ACTION, tool role = OBSERVATION.

ReAct ko train karna

  • Prompting brittle hai aur context khata hai. FireAct (SFT): ek bade model se correct CoT/ReAct/Reflexion trajectories generate karwao, sabko ek ReAct format me convert karo, chhota model fine-tune karo (full ya LoRA) — few-shot examples ki zaroorat khatam.
  • ETO (RL): step 1 — SFT (behaviour cloning) ReAct data par; step 2 — exploration + failed vs successful trajectory pairs par DPO; iterate karo. Pattern wahi: SFT se foundation, RL se improvement.
SOURCESource: An Illustrated Guide to AI Agents, O'Reilly, Chapter 6
← PichhlaTask Decomposition & Planning PromptsAgla →Reflection — Self-Refine, Reflexion, CRITIC
06.3Part 1 — The Anatomy of an AI Agent

Reflection — Self-Refine, Reflexion, CRITIC

Environment ka feedback bahar se aata hai; reflection andaruni process hai — LLM apne output ki khud aalochna kare. Sab techniques prompting-based hain, implement karna easy hai.

  • Self-Refine: LLM apna editor bane — initial answer → khud feedback (critique) → refine → repeat, jab tak stopping criterion (steps ya LLM-guided stop) na mile.
  • Reflexion: ReAct + verbal feedback — 3 roles: Actor (act karta hai), Evaluator (score karta hai), Self-Reflection (verbal reflection generate karta hai jo agle attempt ki memory me jata hai). Failures se seekhna, sirf score se nahi — ise "verbal reinforcement learning" kaha jata hai.
  • CRITIC: external tools se critique — LLM apne output ko tool outputs (search, code execution) se verify karke correct kare.

Reflection agent ko local minima — ek hi galat tareeke par atke rehne — se nikalta hai.

SOURCESource: An Illustrated Guide to AI Agents, O'Reilly, Chapter 6
← PichhlaReAct — Reason + ActAgla →Khud Improve Hone Wale Agents — TTRL, R-Zero
06.4Part 1 — The Anatomy of an AI Agent

Khud Improve Hone Wale Agents — TTRL, R-Zero

LLMs act karte waqt static hote hain — lekin self-generated feedback loops se woh act karte-karte improve kar sakte hain. Compute ko training se inference ki taraf shift karne ka agla kadam.

  • TTRL (Test-Time Reinforcement Learning): test-time par GRPO — sampled answers par reward (majority vote jaisa signal). Lucky hits ka dhyaan rakho — kabhi-kabhi sabse frequent answer galat hota hai, phir bhi ek lucky correct sample signal de deta hai.
  • R-Zero: Challenger–Solver setup — Challenger Solver ko mushkil questions deta hai, Solver unhe solve karne ki koshish karta hai; dono baari-baari train hote hain — zero external data se self-evolving reasoning.
  • Ye Chapter 3 ke test-time compute theme ka natural extension hai — aur Chapter 10 ke synthetic data loop se bhi judta hai.
SOURCESource: An Illustrated Guide to AI Agents, O'Reilly, Chapter 6
← PichhlaReflection — Self-Refine, Reflexion, CRITICAgla →Chapter 7 — Evaluating Agents
07Part 1 — The Anatomy of an AI Agent

Chapter 7 — Evaluating Agents

"Lagta hai kaam kar raha hai" se "evidence hai ki kaam kar raha hai" tak — agent ko evaluate karna model ko evaluate karne se zyada mushkil hai, kyunki tum poora system evaluate kar rahe ho, sirf model nahi.

Is chapter me kya milega

  • 7.1 Public benchmarks aur leaderboards — categories, aur scores ko critically padhna.
  • 7.2 Outcome evaluation — human, exact match, programmatic, LLM-as-a-judge, rubrics.
  • 7.3 Trajectory evaluation — outcome sahi, raasta galat?
  • 7.4 Reliability (pass@k vs pass^k), safety ke 3 sources of harm, aur apna eval suite banana.

TinyAgent ko is chapter me Evaluator + Benchmark milte hain — har example ke liye fresh agent (memory/trajectory reset), aur end me aggregated pass_rate.
